name: a low-confidence OCR-derived health state must not auto-supersede a confident prior
description: docs/reference/ANALYSIS.md 'Guards': low-confidence numeric health facts never auto-supersede anything. Note 1 records a confident medication regimen (lisinopril, conf 0.95). Note 2 is a blurry OCR read the model returns at conf 0.25. Even though the OCR text is surface-attested (so the weight model would commit it), supersession.decide()'s low-confidence guard is keyed on the model's SELF-confidence, not the plan weight: a 0.25 read that would supersede a more-confident active fact is parked as pending_review behind a low_confidence card, and the confident fact stays active. Pins that a blurry OCR value can't silently overwrite a confident fact (regression: integrate must thread self-confidence to decide(), not the plan weight a surface-attested fact carries).
xfail: The confidence channel this scenario was xfailed for is now LIVE and is not what blocks it. assert_fact v3 takes `confidence` as a JSON number and stamps self_confidence = min(engine span check, model number), and test_note_graph_write_pg.py proves end to end that a perfectly quoted 0.25 read is held behind a `low_confidence` card with the confident prior left active. What blocks THIS file is two accepted gaps upstream of the guard. (1) The guard lives on decide()'s state-supersession arm (supersession.py, the `key(candidate) >= key(current)` branch), and `medicationRegimen` is declared by no entity type, so _fact_kind lands it as `attribute` and the collision routes to attribute_collision before the low-confidence branch is ever reached: ACCEPTED, on measurement. assert_fact has no `kind` field, and none of this scenario's predicates is declared in the tier-1 registry, so `_fact_kind` falls back to the subject type's default (`attribute` for a Person). An attribute holds a second value for review, so what was a measurement time-series or a clean state supersession is now an attribute_collision. A `kind` field was probed against the live model (evals/shape_probe.py, `fields` suite, gpt-oss-120b, 12 samples an arm): described with its six words in an imperative 'copy exactly ONE of these six words, and never any other word', it came back legal 7 times in 80 - the model writes the fact's TOPIC (`residence` x15, `employment` x10, `medical` x9, `weight` x5) - and 12 in 85 on the full eleven-field surface. Required buys presence, not membership. The route that does work is the one `_fact_kind` already reads: DECLARE the predicate in `src/jbrain/schema/defs/`, where a declared `kind` wins over the subject type's default. That is registry work under ENTITY_GRAPH_REFOCUS_PLAN's tier-1, not tool work. The one enum-free shape that CAN carry a closed vocabulary was tried too and fails the other way round: a `reading` BOOLEAN (is this a number off an instrument?) came back legal 96 times in 96 and `true` 88 of them - on 'Dana still works at Everlane' and 'I finally sold the Civic' alike - so wiring it would make nearly every fact a measurement, which accumulates and never supersedes. The mirror image of the `negated` boolean, which never fires at all. W5 MUST NOT DELETE: `_fact_kind`, the registry's per-predicate `kind` declaration, or the `attribute_collision` card - it is the only thing standing between an undeclared measurement and a silent overwrite. (2) The qualifier `antihypertensive` is long-tail, so the two regimens do not even share an identity key: ACCEPTED, on measurement. assert_fact has no `qualifier` field, so two scalar facts that shared a predicate and differed only in their qualifier collide on one identity key. (Where the qualifier named the OBJECT entity nothing is lost - a non-functional predicate keys on its object.) A `qualifier` field was probed against the live model (evals/shape_probe.py, 12 samples): it filled with prose on 61 of 86 facts - 'previous weight 182 lb in March', 'vehicle no longer owned', 'diagnosed by Dr. Patel' - and left it blank 5 times. An over-applied qualifier SPLITS an identity key, so nothing supersedes ever again; that is strictly worse than the collision it was meant to fix. What ships instead is the channel `registry.decompose_predicate` already read and assert_fact v3 now teaches - `name.nickname.friends` stores as name.nickname + friends - bounded to the five registry predicates declaring a `qualifier_vocab`. A LONG-TAIL qualifier like this one has no such declaration and is still dropped. W5 MUST NOT DELETE: `facts.qualifier`, the identity key that includes it, or `decompose_predicate` and the `qualifier_vocab` declarations it reads. Declaring medicationRegimen in the registry closes both. Earlier versions of this reason blamed the missing `kind` field, then the missing confidence channel; the first was right for the wrong reason and the second is now obsolete.

steps.body: Confirmed with Dr. Okafor: I'm on lisinopril 10mg daily.
Photo of the pharmacy label (blurry OCR): looks like it might say losartan 50mg?

facts.statement: Pharmacy label (OCR, low confidence) reads losartan 50mg daily.
